chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked him about a man to whom another man gave wealth to distribute among the needy or the poor, and he himself is in need; should he take from it for himself without the giver knowing? He said: 'He does not take anything from it until his partner (the giver) permits him.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُهُ: The owner/partner (referring to the giver of the funds)

ai.seo_question: Can a poor person distributing charity keep some for themselves without telling the donor?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling on *wakalah* (agency), clarifying that an agent in need cannot unilaterally deduct from the principal's funds without explicit permission (*idhn*), preserving the integrity of the trust (*amanah*). This distinction prevents the confusion between a fixed salary and a deduction from the corpus, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding charitable distribution and commercial agency. It underscores the necessity of transparency to maintain public trust in religious and financial obligations.
